app_documentation:
Simple Task Manager is a web-based task management application designed to help users efficiently track and organize their daily work activities. Built with modern web technologies including React for the frontend and Node.js/Express for the backend, the application provides a clean, intuitive interface for managing personal tasks. The system uses PostgreSQL as its database to ensure reliable data persistence and supports user authentication to maintain individual task lists securely.

The application's core functionality revolves around four primary features: Task Creation allows users to create new tasks with titles and optional descriptions; Task Completion enables users to mark tasks as complete or reopen them as needed; Task Deletion provides the ability to permanently remove unwanted tasks with confirmation safeguards; and Task List View displays all tasks in an organized format with filtering capabilities to separate completed and incomplete items. The interface follows a mobile-first design approach with responsive layouts that adapt seamlessly across web browsers on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

Intended for individual users who need a straightforward solution for personal task management, Simple Task Manager emphasizes usability and accessibility. The application implements WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, ensuring that users with disabilities can effectively navigate and use all features. With a calming color palette, clear visual hierarchy, and touch-friendly components, the app reduces cognitive load while maintaining professional aesthetics. Users can view task statistics, manage their profile information, and benefit from smooth animations and transitions that enhance the overall user experience without causing distraction.

The technical architecture leverages a RESTful API design pattern, with the Express backend handling authentication, data validation, and database operations, while the React frontend manages state, routing, and component rendering. The PostgreSQL database schema maintains referential integrity through foreign key relationships between users and their tasks, with proper indexing on frequently queried fields to ensure optimal performance. This architecture supports future scalability and feature enhancements while maintaining a clean separation of concerns between presentation, business logic, and data layers.

glossary.Task: A discrete work item created by a user with a required title and optional description that can be marked as complete or incomplete, edited, or deleted. Tasks are stored in the database with timestamps tracking creation and modification dates.
glossary.FAB (Floating Action Button): A circular button positioned in the bottom-right corner of the Task List screen that serves as the primary action trigger for creating new tasks. It features a plus icon and uses the application's primary color with an elevated shadow effect.
glossary.Task Completion Status: A boolean flag (is_completed) stored in the database that indicates whether a task has been finished. Users can toggle this status through checkbox interactions in the task list or detail views, with visual feedback including strikethrough text and color changes.
glossary.Modal Overlay: A semi-transparent full-screen layer that appears over the main interface to display focused content such as the Delete Confirmation dialog. Users can dismiss modals by tapping outside the modal card or using cancel actions.
glossary.Baseline Artifact: A versioned snapshot of project documentation including requirements, design specifications, database schemas, and execution plans that serves as a reference point for tracking changes and maintaining project governance throughout the development lifecycle.
glossary.Acceptance Criteria: Specific, testable conditions defined in Given-When-Then format that must be met for a feature to be considered complete and functioning as intended. These criteria guide development and testing efforts to ensure features meet user expectations and business requirements.
